title: Rapid Canary Fire-Drill Playbook for Sellers (Sketch)
body:
Audience: platform-focused sellers + solutions engineers + quick-response CS. Purpose: give a 3–6 slide sequencing + speaker notes to lead a live canary ‘fire-drill’ during pilot/proof-of-concept handoff. This is intentionally lightweight — scripted prompts, decision triggers, and an emergency fallback checklist so sellers can own uptime confidence during early production traffic.

Slide 1 — One-liner + why it matters
• Title: Canary Fire-Drill: A 10–15 minute tactical runbook for sellers.
• Speaker notes: Open by setting expectation: quick, repeatable, and low-risk. Explain that this is not an SRE deep-dive; it’s a sales-ops ritual to validate customer readiness and build trust. Mention typical trigger: first 1k–10k tokens or first 100 requests in a new route/region.

Slide 2 — Quick diagnostics (pre-flight ~3 min)
• Checklist bullets: Verify model version pinned, route policy (primary + fallback) is set, auth token and quota are present, dedicated capacity or planned capacity mapping, telemetry streaming enabled. Confirm region match.
• Speaker notes: Walk seller through a 5-question script to ask the customer (or internal SE): 1) Which endpoint will be used? 2) Expected peak concurrent users? 3) Is there a business impact window and rollback tolerance? 4) Do we have an example payload with typical sequence length? 5) Any IP/proxy/network constraints? Use answers to set SLOs for the canary.

Slide 3 — Canary scenario matrix (2–3 rapid scenarios)
• Scenario A: Low-volume functional validation (latency not critical). Goal: verify correctness, output shape, and auth.
• Scenario B: Latency-sensitive path (UI or sync API). Goal: measure p50/p95 under small synthetic concurrency.
• Scenario C: Throughput pressure (batch jobs or background embeddings). Goal: validate throughput and fallback behavior when capacity is saturated.
• Speaker notes: For each scenario, call out the single metric to watch (A: correctness checks/errors, B: p95 latency, C: tail QPS and token-per-second). Provide short commands or curl snippets to run a 10-request smoke test and a 60s mini-load.

Slide 4 — Automated fallback and escalation triggers (decision tree)
• Trigger thresholds (examples): error rate > 2% over 1 minute; p95 latency > SLA * 2 for 60s; sustained queue/backlog growth for 120s.
• Immediate seller action: flip to fallback route (documented name), notify SE, create Incident stub with tag canary/<customer>-<date>.
• Speaker notes: Emphasize that sellers are authorized to flip to documented fallback routes for customer-facing demos and pilots. Include precise path names for common fallback models (e.g., gpt-small-compat -> gpt-medium-fallback) and mention auto-rollback windows.

Slide 5 — Emergency checklist (5 items)
• 1) Switch routing to fallback model (who/how).
• 2) Reduce concurrency / rate-limit the pilot user.
• 3) Enable verbose debug trace and collect the last 10 request IDs.
• 4) Open an urgent ticket and ping on #prod-canary with incident stub.
• 5) Schedule a synchronous huddle and propose next-step window (30–60 min).
• Speaker notes: Keep this short — sellers should be able to execute in <3 minutes. Include a sample Slack snippet and an Incident title template.

Slide 6 — Post-mortem micro-template + customer messaging
• Post-mortem fields: timeline, root cause hypothesis, impact (time + user count), mitigation applied, next steps. Keep the official template under confluence:CANARY-PLAYBOOK-2025.
• Customer messaging samples: three short templates — (A) Successful run: quick summary emphasizing performance and next milestones. (B) Minor degradation: apology + what we rolled back + timeline for fix. (C) Major outage: escalation to SE/CS leadership and offer for meeting within 2 hours.

Appendix (speaker cheat-sheet) — actionable snippets and quick links
• curl snippet (smoke test): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"<model>","input":"<sample>"}'
• mini-load script (60s): python snippet for parallel requests (two-thread example).
• Quick metric targets: p50 < 150ms (small models), p95 < 600ms (medium), error < 1% for demo-mode.
• Links: Confluence (CANARY-PLAYBOOK-2025), Jira INF-8721 (canary automation backlog), GitHub PR 3412 (routing SDK fixes).

Open questions / to-do (for this draft)
• Should sellers be allowed to natively initiate a regional failover or only request SE? Recommend: allow sellers for demo/pilot, require SE approval for dedicated capacity migrations.
• Do we need an automated rollback if canary error spikes beyond threshold? Proposed: yes — short window 30–120s configurable per account.
• Actions for next iteration: add automated telemetry dashboard link per-customer + pre-populated incident templates.

Why this is different (notes to reviewer)
• This playbook explicitly centers the seller’s role in a controlled canary, not as a replacement for SRE. The focus is enabling sellers to confidently run short, readable validations with clear escape hatches and customer messaging. It prioritizes short response time and repeatability over deep troubleshooting.

Revision history: 2025-11-04 initial sketch by Asha K., 2025-11-12 added triggers and sample scripts (Diego M.), 2025-11-20 editorial pass and customer messaging (Priya N.).
